articles.title: 3 expert-approved KN95 masks to keep you healthy this season
articles.summary: KN95 masks can offer the best protection against Covid, according to the CDC. We asked experts how to wear KN95 masks, plus the best brands to shop from.
articles.body: Fewer people wear face masks than during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, but they’re still great personal protective equipment to keep at home. They can help prevent illness and protect the people around you, especially if you’re experiencing cold or flu symptoms. There are many face masks to choose from, but according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, properly fitting respirators offer the most protection. Experts say N95 respirators are the gold standard of face masks, but some people find them uncomfortable. High-quality KN95 masks, which offer similar protection, can be a more comfortable alternative. After speaking with experts for tips on buying KN95 masks, I found a handful of options that meet their criteria. Plus, I bought and tried all of the face masks below to ensure their packaging, features and fit align with what experts say to expect. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best KN95 masks Best overall These Hotodeal masks were included on the FDA's EUA list. They come in a packs of 20, 40, 60 and 120, and are built with an adjustable nose bridge and stretchy ear loops. The masks come in colors like white, black and grey. Best neutral colors Powecom’s KN95 masks were featured on the FDA’s EUA list. They are available in black and white, as well as multiple colors, all of which come in a pack of 10. You can also purchase individually packaged KN95s. The masks have an adjustable nose piece and their ear loops are latex-free, according to the brand. Best to buy in bulk WellBefore offers KN95 masks in multiple colors and lets you choose between standard ear loops and head straps. The masks have an adjustable nose bridge, and you can purchase as few as 10 masks, which come individually wrapped. Note: The price listed above reflects the cost of 10 KN95 masks with standard ear loops. You must purchase a minimum of 10 masks per order. How I picked the best KN95 masks Here are the factors I kept in mind to create our list: Filtration level: Experts told me that KN95 masks must filter out at least 95% of particulates. For all of the masks I recommend, I obtained associated lab tests regarding filtration. I got documentation from the NIOSH National Personal Protective Technology Laboratory or had brands send me documentation directly.Construction: The KN95 masks you buy should have ear loops and at least five layers of material. All of the masks above are designed with these features, as well as an adjustable nose bridge.Brand transparency: Brand transparency is key when buying any type of face mask, especially for KN95 masks, which the U.S. does not regulate the way it does for N95 masks. There are, however, ways for brands and manufacturers to increase their trustworthiness, like FDA registration or inclusion in the FDA’s now-defunct emergency use authorization (EUA), which it passed in 2020 to help medical workers choose KN95 masks when there was a shortage of N95 masks. All of the masks I recommend come from manufacturers registered with the FDA — while this has nothing to do with regulating mask quality, it increases accountability for the brand selling it, experts told me. Some of the masks I recommend also appeared on the FDA’s EUA — I note which ones. How to shop for KN95 masks It’s difficult, if not impossible, to be sure that the KN95 mask you’re buying is real just by looking at it, says Dr. Jeremy Friese, a former Mayo Clinic physician and founder and CEO of Humata Health. To help guide your shopping, the CDC offers a list of tips to help you spot masks that may not meet the necessary standards. Experts I interviewed recommend reviewing your masks before wearing them with the following in mind: When you take a KN95 mask out of its packaging, it should not be damaged in any way.Packaging should never include false claims or logos from the FDA. The FDA does not permit their logo to appear on packaging of any sort.KN95 masks shouldn’t cost more than $3 a piece, according to the CDC. You should also review lab testing documents that clearly illustrate how well a mask acts as a filter before you use it, says Anne Miller, executive director of Project N95, a nonprofit that helps people source personal protective equipment and medical supplies. Some brands publish these documents online, while others may send you them if you ask. Another factor to consider while shopping for KN95 masks is FDA registration. To register with the FDA, manufacturers pay a fee and submit certain criteria about their business. Though this is better to have than not, FDA registration has no bearing on the quality of the face mask itself, and it does not denote FDA approval of the mask or its manufacturer. Miller also says the list of KN95 models the FDA specifically approved in its 2020 emergency use authorization is one of the best resources to use when sourcing the respirators, even after the FDA stopped updating the list in 2021. What is a KN95 mask? A KN95 face mask is a type of disposable respirator. (Most people use “mask” and “respirator” interchangeably, but when the CDC and medical professionals say “respirator,” they specifically mean specialized, fitted face coverings like N95s, KN95s and KF94s.) It filters 95% of particulate matter, just like the N95 mask, says Dr. Nina Shapiro, a pediatric ear, nose and throat specialist at Westside Head and Neck in California. KN95 masks are the Chinese equivalent of an N95 respirator in the U.S. A Chinese governing body similar to the U.S. National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health sets the standard for KN95 masks in China. Since they’re designed to meet a Chinese standard, KN95s are not regulated in the U.S. From April 2020 to June 2021, the FDA had a temporary emergency use authorization that allowed U.S. health workers to use KN95s on the job. It later ended the EUA because NIOSH-approved respirators were no longer in short supply. When should you wear a face mask? Currently, there are no state- or city-wide masking regulations in the U.S. However, wearing a face mask, be it a KN95 or another type, can help protect you from viruses like COVID-19, the flu and the common cold, as well as prevent you from spreading illness if you're experiencing symptoms. This is especially true during annual flu season and busy summer travel seasons. The highest risk settings for viral spread are crowded indoor environments like airplanes, trains, busses and concert venues, says Shapiro. She also recommends wearing a face mask in waiting areas at doctors' offices or hospitals, since viruses tend to frequently circulate in these settings. If you’re exhibiting symptoms of a respiratory illness like coughing, sneezing or a fever, you should stay home and not spend time in public spaces, says Shapiro. But if you have to leave your home to visit the doctor or pick up medication, for example, it's best to wear a face mask to protect those around you. Meet our health experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts with specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also ensure that all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and with no undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Dr. Nina Shapiro is a pediatric ear, nose and throat specialist at Westside Head and Neck in California. She is the author of “Hype: A Doctor’s Guide To Medical Myths, Exaggerated Claims and Bad Advice,” as well as a children’s book, “The Ultimate Kids’ Guide To Being Super Healthy.”Dr. Jeremy Friese is a former Mayo Clinic physician and the founder and CEO of Humata Health.Anne Miller is the executive director of Project N95, a nonprofit that helps people source personal protective equipment and medical supplies. Why trust NBC Selected? I'm a reporter at NBC Selected who has covered face masks since 2020. I've written about disposable masks, KN95 masks, N95 masks and KN95 masks for kids, in addition to at-home COVID-19 tests and vaccine card holders. For this article, I spoke to three experts about how to shop for KN95 masks and tried every mask I recommend. articles.title: Morte de 5 macacos-prego em Pastos Bons é investigada | G1
articles.standfirst: Amostras dos animais encontrados na zona rural foram enviadas ao Laboratório Central de Saúde Pública do Maranhão (Lacen-MA). Os exames devem esclarecer o que provocou as mortes.
articles.summary: Amostras dos animais encontrados na zona rural foram enviadas ao Laboratório Central de Saúde Pública do Maranhão (Lacen-MA). Os exames devem esclarecer o que provocou as mortes.
articles.body:
A morte de cinco macacos-prego no município de Pastos Bons , no interior do Maranhão, está sendo investigada por equipes de saúde e meio ambiente. Entre as hipóteses analisadas estão a febre amarela, a raiva e possíveis causas ambientais. Amostras dos animais foram encaminhadas ao Laboratório Central de Saúde Pública do Maranhão (Lacen-MA).

Os primeiros macacos foram encontrados por moradores de um povoado na zona rural do município, no domingo (18). Na segunda-feira (19), outros dois animais morreram. O quinto macaco chegou a ser resgatado com sinais de debilidade, mas não resistiu.

Após ser informada sobre o caso, a Prefeitura de Pastos Bons enviou equipes das áreas de saúde e meio ambiente ao local para recolher amostras e iniciar a investigação.

Uma das primeiras suspeitas era de que os animais tivessem morrido após sofrer descargas elétricas da rede de energia que passa próximo à área de mata onde foram encontrados. No entanto, os exames externos não conseguiram comprovar essa possibilidade.

Diante da suspeita de doenças infecciosas, amostras de órgãos internos dos macacos foram encaminhadas ao Lacen-MA. Os exames devem ajudar a identificar se as mortes estão relacionadas à febre amarela, à raiva ou a outras causas.

Mortes de macacos podem indicar circulação da febre amarela

Segundo o infectologista Daniel Wagner, os macacos são considerados sentinelas da febre amarela, porque podem adoecer e morrer antes mesmo da identificação de casos da doença em humanos.

Por isso, a morte de vários animais em uma mesma região é considerada um sinal de alerta e precisa ser investigada pelas autoridades de saúde.

"Os macacos, na verdade, são as sentinelas da febre amarela. Eles podem adoecer e morrer antes mesmo de identificarmos os casos humanos. Por isso, a febre amarela é uma das principais hipóteses infecciosas que precisam ser investigadas no cenário de Pastos Bons. A raiva também deve ser considerada, mas a morte de vários macacos ao mesmo tempo, nesse período, não é um padrão característico da doença. Outras causas ambientais também precisam ser investigadas", explicou o infectologista.

A causa das mortes ainda não foi confirmada e depende dos resultados das análises laboratoriais.

articles.title: Incêndio em fábrica de plástico em Limeira: vídeo mostra chamas | G1
articles.standfirst: Caso foi registrado na manhã desta sexta-feira (23) em fábrica que fica no cruzamento da Avenida Dezoito com a Rua Caminho da Servidão. Não houve feridos.
articles.summary: Um incêndio em fábrica de plástico em Limeira mobilizou o Corpo de Bombeiros no bairro Ferrão nesta sexta-feira (23), sem deixar feridos no local.
articles.body:
Uma fábrica de plástico pegou fogo na manhã desta sexta-feira (23) no bairro do Ferrão em Limeira (SP). Segundo Corpo de Bombeiros, não houve registro de feridos. O fogo chamou atenção de moradores que frequentam a região. Imagens do incêndio foram registradas em vídeo pela população. Assista, acima.

A fábrica de plástico fica no cruzamento da Avenida Dezoito com a Rua Caminho da Servidão. Cerca de cinco equipes dos Corpo de Bombeiros trabalharam no combate às chamas no local.

Segundo o relato recebido pelos bombeiros, esta não é a primeira vez que a fábrica é atingido por incêndios.

Consultada pela EPTV , afiliada da Globo para Piracicaba e região, a Prefeitura de Limeira informou que a Defesa Civil informou que não foi acionada para atender à ocorrência.

Não há informações sobre o alvará de funcionamento da empresa.

articles.title: Macron classifica tiroteio na França como ato 'terrorista e racista' | G1
articles.standfirst: Suspeito abriu fogo de dentro de um veículo e foi preso cerca de 10 quilômetros depois do ponto em que fez o primeiro ataque.
articles.summary: Após ataque em Paris deixar um morto e feridos, Emmanuel Macron afirma que o crime teve motivação terrorista e racista; suspeito foi detido pelas autoridades.
articles.body:
O presidente da França , Emmanuel Macron, afirmou que o tiroteio em duas cidades nos arredores de Paris nesta sexta-feira (23) foi um ataque "terrorista" e "racista". A informação é da agência Reuters.

Um homem armado matou uma pessoa e feriu outras quatro no ataque.

Mais cedo, pelo X (antigo Twitter), Macron prestou solidariedade aos familiares das vítimas e afirmou que o homem já havia sido preso.

Presidente da França, Emmanuel Macron, em coletiva de imprensa no Catar em 21 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Benoit Tessier/Pool

"Profunda emoção após o ataque a tiros ocorrido em Trappes e La Verrière [...] Nossos pensamentos estão com as vítimas, suas famílias, bem como com todos os habitantes dos Yvelines. Nesta terrível provação, a Nação está ao lado delas."

O suspeito estava dentro de um veículo quando disparou os tiros , por volta das 10h30 do horário local - 5h30 em Brasília -, em Trappes, comuna a cerca de 30 quilômetros a oeste de Paris.

Depois, ele seguiu La Verrière, cerca de 5 quilômetros distante da cidade, e foi preso em Coignières, quatro quilômetros à frente.

Perícia sendo feita em um dos locais onde tiros foram disparados contra pedestres por motorista na França — Foto: BFM TV via REUTERS

"Houve inúmeros tiroteios, em diferentes partes da cidade. O atirador claramente estava disparando aleatoriamente e queria causar carnificina", afirmou o prefeito de Trappes, Ali Rabeh, em entrevista à BFM.

Segundo o prefeito de La Verrière, Nicolas Dainville, uma criança de 12 anos faz parte do grupo de feridos e foi atingida oito vezes, mas seu estado de saúde no momento é estável.

Dois outros feridos são homens - um na casa dos 20 e o outro de 49. Eles foram levados para o hospital, mas não correm risco de morte.

Na rede social X, o primeiro-ministro da França anunciou que o crime está sendo investigado pela Procuradoria Nacional Antiterrorista:

"Acabou de ocorrer um incidente muito grave em Trappes, no departamento de Yvelines. Uma pessoa morreu e quatro ficaram feridas. O indivíduo foi detido e está sob custódia. Todos os recursos disponíveis das forças de segurança e das autoridades judiciais estão totalmente mobilizados. A Procuradoria Nacional Antiterrorista anunciou que está monitorando a situação. As autoridades competentes comunicarão mais informações oportunamente", escreveu.

Pouco depois, os procuradores afirmaram que investigam o caso como um "homicídio relacionado a uma organização terrorista".

De acordo com o deputado Laurent Mazaury, o suspeito foi detido no estacionamento de uma loja Kiloutou, em uma área comercial.

articles.title: Florianópolis amplia atendimento odontológico com novos serviços e tecnologias | G1
articles.standfirst: Rede municipal realizou mais de 422 mil procedimentos em 2025 e investe em atendimento especializado, unidades móveis e ampliação das equipes de Saúde Bucal
articles.summary: Rede municipal realizou mais de 422 mil procedimentos em 2025 e investe em atendimento especializado, unidades móveis e ampliação das equipes de Saúde Bucal
articles.body:
A rede municipal de saúde de Florianópolis está ampliando os serviços odontológicos para atender às diferentes necessidades da população. Entre as iniciativas estão a implantação de laserterapia nos Centros de Saúde, atendimento odontológico para pessoas trans, indígenas e em situação de rua, aquisição de uma unidade móvel e oferta de procedimentos sob sedação para pacientes com necessidades especiais. As medidas também incluem reformas nos Centros de Especialidades Odontológicas (CEOs) e ampliação das equipes de Saúde Bucal.

Somente em 2025, a rede municipal realizou mais de 422 mil procedimentos odontológicos. A Prefeitura, por meio da Secretaria Municipal de Saúde, pretende ampliar a cobertura dos serviços e facilitar o acesso ao atendimento, principalmente para pessoas que enfrentam dificuldades para chegar às unidades de saúde ou necessitam de cuidados específicos.

Atendimento chega a novos públicos e territórios

Uma das frentes de ampliação é o atendimento odontológico no Ambulatório Trans, destinado a pessoas trans, travestis e não binárias de qualquer idade que residam em Florianópolis. O serviço integra a assistência já oferecida pelo ambulatório e busca garantir um atendimento adequado às necessidades desse público.

A iniciativa também funciona como campo de estágio para cirurgiões-dentistas do Programa de Residência Multiprofissional em Saúde da Família.

Na aldeia urbana do Saco dos Limões, a população indígena passou a receber atendimento odontológico no próprio território, por meio de uma parceria com a Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina (UFSC). O trabalho inclui ações preventivas, educação em saúde, diagnóstico precoce de problemas bucais e atendimentos feitos na aldeia e na UFSC.

Já para as pessoas em situação de rua, a assistência ocorre por meio do Consultório na Rua, que oferece atendimento odontológico diretamente nos territórios onde essa população se encontra.

A proposta é reduzir barreiras de acesso e aproximar os serviços de saúde das pessoas que, por diferentes motivos, têm dificuldade de procurar atendimento nas unidades convencionais.

Laserterapia e Odontomóvel estão entre as novidades

A incorporação de novas tecnologias também faz parte da expansão. A Atenção Primária à Saúde Bucal passou a contar com a laserterapia, inicialmente em formato de projeto-piloto.

O recurso pode ser utilizado em diferentes situações clínicas, como recuperação pós-operatória, sensibilidade dentária, lesões na boca e procedimentos de frenectomia em recém-nascidos. Também poderá auxiliar pacientes em tratamento oncológico, contribuindo para o controle de feridas e desconfortos provocados pela quimioterapia e radioterapia.

Florianópolis amplia atendimento odontológico — Foto: Divulgação/PMF

Outra novidade é a aquisição de um Odontomóvel, uma van equipada com consultório odontológico completo. A unidade móvel deverá começar a funcionar ainda em 2026 e será utilizada para levar atendimento a regiões com maior necessidade ou dificuldade de acesso aos Centros de Saúde.

O veículo também poderá participar de atividades em escolas e campanhas de promoção da saúde bucal.

“Isso significa investir em prevenção e diagnóstico precoce, levar o atendimento para mais perto de quem tem dificuldade de acesso, incorporar novas tecnologias e qualificar os serviços especializados. A proposta é fortalecer uma rede mais integrada, capaz de acompanhar o paciente em diferentes momentos do cuidado e oferecer respostas mais adequadas para cada necessidade”, explica a chefe da Divisão de Saúde Bucal, Valeska Maddalozzo Pivatto.

Centros especializados passam por reformas

Os Centros de Especialidades Odontológicas das regiões Central e Continental também estão passando por reestruturação. As intervenções incluem melhorias na infraestrutura, substituição de equipamentos antigos e adequação dos ambientes para ampliar a qualidade dos atendimentos.

Entre as mudanças já realizadas está a criação de um espaço exclusivo e ampliado para pacientes com necessidades especiais, integrado a uma sala de repouso para o período posterior aos procedimentos.

A rede também está digitalizando os exames de radiografia odontológica. A medida busca agilizar a realização dos exames, facilitar o armazenamento e o compartilhamento das imagens e reduzir o uso de materiais associados aos métodos convencionais.

No MultiHospital, outra frente já implantada é o atendimento odontológico sob sedação para pacientes com necessidades especiais que precisam de suporte hospitalar.

O serviço é destinado a situações em que o atendimento convencional não é possível ou apresenta riscos clínicos. Entre os públicos contemplados estão pessoas com Transtorno do Espectro Autista (TEA), doenças neurológicas e degenerativas graves, transtornos psiquiátricos, ansiedade severa e outras condições que exigem acompanhamento e monitoramento durante os procedimentos.

Ampliação das equipes busca acompanhar crescimento da cidade

Além das novas modalidades de atendimento, a Secretaria Municipal de Saúde trabalha na recomposição das equipes de Saúde Bucal e no preenchimento de vagas existentes.

A administração municipal também realiza o planejamento de novos territórios prioritários para ampliar a cobertura odontológica, considerando o crescimento populacional e a demanda pelos serviços.

Outra medida em desenvolvimento é uma solução digital para o agendamento de consultas, com o objetivo de facilitar o acesso dos pacientes e organizar os fluxos de atendimento.

As mudanças abrangem desde a prevenção e o atendimento odontológico nos bairros até procedimentos especializados, com a proposta de ampliar a capacidade da rede municipal e oferecer assistência adequada às diferentes necessidades da população.

Conforme Lei nº 10.199, a Prefeitura informa que a produção deste conteúdo não teve custo e sua veiculação custou em média R$ 2.550,00.

articles.title: Capivaras viram sensação em Palmas e conquistam moradores e turistas | G1
articles.standfirst: Presentes em áreas verdes de Palmas, as capivaras encontraram refúgio no Parque Cesamar. Apesar da proximidade, os animais devem ser respeitados e não devem ser tocados.
articles.summary: Presentes em áreas verdes de Palmas, as capivaras encontraram refúgio no Parque Cesamar. Apesar da proximidade, os animais devem ser respeitados e não devem ser tocados.
articles.body:
A capivara conquistou um lugar especial no coração dos palmenses. Presente em áreas verdes de Palmas , o animal virou inspiração para pelúcias, camisetas, ímãs e até para pastel com formato do animal.

Com focinho redondo e jeito tranquilo, a capivara virou estrela das vitrines. Em uma loja de pelúcias, o bichinho pode ganhar camisa, macacão, tênis e até bolsa. Quem monta a pelúcia escolhe cada acessório e a procura é tão grande que o estoque precisa ser reposto com frequência.

"A capivara é um produto que a gente não consegue ficar sem por conta da demanda realmente, que é muito alta", afirmou Maria Eduarda.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

No Parque Cesamar, a inspiração aparece ao vivo, sem precisar de propaganda. As capivaras chamam a atenção de quem caminha, passeia ou visita a cidade.

O lago do parque e o Córrego Brejo Comprido criam um ambiente favorável para a espécie. A água serve de refúgio, ajuda na locomoção, na regulação da temperatura e faz parte do ciclo de vida desses animais.

Capivara de pelúcia é sucesso de vendas em Palmas — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhanguera

Essa especialista explica que, com o tempo, as capivaras também passaram a tolerar mais a presença humana. Mas essa aparente tranquilidade não é um convite para a aproximação.

"E a gente sempre fala, o animal ele não sabe o que que você quer, ele não sabe o que que você vai fazer. Então ele pode, pra se defender, acabar mordendo, acabar, é, fazendo alguma coisa que possa machucar", explicou Bruna de Almeida, diretora de manejo e proteção da fauna silvestre de Palmas.

Na Praia da Graciosa, a febre ganhou sabor. A Morgana criou um pastel em homenagem à capivara e colocou uma versão inflável na porta para receber os clientes. A estratégia virou atração, principalmente entre as crianças.

"Nós trabalhamos com os ingredientes regionais do Tocantins e a representatividade do Tocantins e do município de Palmas. E a capivara é um símbolo, se tornou um símbolo nacional, mas também de Palmas, porque nós temos o Parque Cesamar. E por esse motivo a gente quis homenagear e trouxemos o pastel no formato de capivara", contou Morgana Lima Martins.

articles.title: Hadi Alodid: Man charged over Belfast knife attack pleads not guilty
articles.summary: A man charged in connection with a knife attack in north Belfast, that sparked serious disorder in the city, pleads not guilty to attempted murder.
articles.body:
A man charged in connection with a knife attack in north Belfast that sparked serious disorder in the city has pleaded not guilty to attempted murder.

Hadi Alodid, 31, of Duncairn Avenue in Belfast, has also denied possessing a bladed weapon and a charge of threatening or abusive behaviour.

Alodid is accused of carrying out the attack on Stephen Ogilvie in June.

Stephen Ogilvie, who is in his 40s, lost his left eye in the incident and sustained damage to his right.

Alodid, who has been in custody since the attack, was led into the dock in handcuffs at Belfast Crown Court, where three charges were put to him.

Dressed in a grey prison tracksuit, Alodid stood with his arms folded as an Arabic interpreter translated the proceedings for him.

He responded to all three charges in English with the words "not guilty".

A date was set for his trial in early February.

A number of review hearings will be held prior to that.

The attack, which the court heard took place in the vicinity of Kinnaird Avenue in north Belfast, happened on June 8.

Videos circulating online at the time showed a number of people, including one wielding a hurling stick, confronting the apparent attacker until police arrived.

Alodid was arrested at the scene and remanded into custody.

Following the attack, violence erupted across Belfast, which saw homes and vehicles set alight.

articles.title: Her 6-year-old brought home an AI-generated photo from school. This mom isn’t having it
articles.summary: Nikki Anderson's 6-year-old daughter brought home from school an AI-generated photo of herself at age 25. Anderson was furious.
articles.body:
When Nikki Anderson, 32, opened up her 6-year-old's Friday folder on Oct. 16, she was excited to see what her daughter , Harper, had been working on at school that week.

The folder contained spelling tests and artwork from Harper's first grade classroom. But among the construction paper and lined sheets where her daughter wrote what she wanted to be when she grows up − a nurse − was a peculiar photo that stopped Anderson in her tracks.

The image, generated by artificial intelligence, showed what her daughter would look like as a 25-year-old. The image was of a young woman with a "baby face," Anderson said, with sleek, wavy hair, wearing a nurse's uniform and holding a clipboard. Anderson's daughter proudly told her mother how her specials teacher had made the photo with AI. She especially loved the wavy hair she'd have when she's a grownup, Harper said.

Another image of her daughter as a nurse − the one her daughter dreamed up with her own imagination and crafted with her own two hands out of construction paper and penciled-in eyes, nose and mouth − didn't feature wavy hair.

"My child's interpretation of the world has been replaced with an algorithm's interpretation of what a successful adult woman should look like," Anderson, of Charleston, South Carolina, wrote in an Instagram post about the AI image, which has more than 600,000 likes. "She had already imagined the future. Made something incredible to represent it. What part of that needed to be finished by a computer?"

AI is infiltrating everyday life, and the classroom is no exception. Many teachers are adapting to AI use , urged by some education leaders to not get left behind. Even in places prohibiting AI use in some classrooms – like New York City, where Mayor Zohran Mamdani mandated it as such for preschool through eighth grade students in September – teachers are pushing back by saying students need to learn how to use AI in safe and smart ways. But is AI use in schools getting in the way of children's creativity? And shouldn't parents have to give permission before images of their kids are uploaded onto AI platforms? These are the questions Anderson and thousands of other parents are asking in the wake of the AI boom.

There's a lack of legislation and guidance around AI use in schools and what teachers should or shouldn't put into AI models, said Tina Mulqueen, a professor at Washington State University Vancouver and senior vice president of digital transformation at Burson, a communications company.

"I don't want to put that on the teacher," she said. "I just have so much respect for teachers. It's a really difficult job and I think that most of them are really well-intentioned in how they're trying to navigate this with AI."

Teachers shouldn't be inserting personally identifiable information about students into AI models, Mulqueen said. But if AI is going to be useful and expected in the workforce, she said, "then we probably want to teach our kids to be able to interface."

"But we don't want to take learning away from them," she said.

Conversations around AI in classrooms are typically centered around AI literacy and how to use AI to improve learning, said Jason Yeh, cofounder of Patron, an early stage venture firm investing in the next generation of consumer technology. One of his investments is in a company that specializes in personalized education through AI. But Anderson's situation doesn't sound related to either of those purposes, he said. Because parents are growing increasingly wary of AI, Yeh said more and more schools are becoming cautious about using it at all.

"Schools need to figure out the best way to incorporate relevant technology to help people learn better," Yeh said.

Anderson told USA TODAY she signed a consent form at the start of the school year that allowed the school to use Harper's photos and artwork in the media; it didn't say anything about AI.

"Charleston County School District recognizes both the opportunities and responsibilities that come with the use of artificial intelligence in education, particularly when it involves student images and personal information," Harper's school district provided in an emailed statement to USA TODAY, adding that the district has established policies and guidance surrounding responsible use of technology and partnered with AI for Education, a national consulting organization, beginning in 2025 to develop an AI framework . "Once concerns were brought to the school's attention, the principal directed that similar assignments be discontinued, and the district followed its established procedures to address the matter."

The district is preparing to launch comprehensive, districtwide AI literacy training for educators in the coming weeks to reinforce expectations about student privacy, approved AI tools, ethical use and appropriate instructional practices, the district said.

Anderson said she is "pretty against AI" as it pertains to child development, and she's worried about privacy concerns. She's read about increased child sex abuse materials being made available with AI, and said "all parents are just kind of on high alert right now because we're trying to protect our kids' imagination and privacy."

Yeh uses AI with his children at home sometimes, with parent supervision, and sees many ways AI can be useful in educational situations. He, too, said he'd be concerned if either of his elementary-aged children came home with a similar image to the one Harper's teacher made.

"It's hard to imagine how that ties into something that they would be learning," he said.

Anderson said she doesn't think Harper's teacher did anything malicious, and that the idea of the assignment was sweet in some ways. She's also aware teachers "are overworked, underpaid, just absolutely fighting to do their best with kids and I absolutely want them to have access to material that makes them feel like they can better manage their schedules," including AI tools.

But she doesn't want her daughter interfacing with AI at 6 years old. She said she struggled to have that conversation with her daughter when it came up. "I want her to think that science and advancement is fascinating and it's necessary and it's useful," she said. For now, though, Anderson is focusing on the art Harper makes herself.

"How your hair looks whenever you're 25, I promise you, is going to be the least important thing about you," she told her daughter.

articles.title: At least seven killed after gunmen open fire at church in Jordan
articles.summary: Survivors say two masked men began shooting as dozens attended a funeral procession.
articles.body:
At least seven people have been killed, and 34 others wounded, in an attack in Jordan’s Karak governorate that saw gunmen open fire during a funeral at a church.

Director of Jordan’s Public Security Directorate Obaidullah Al-Maaytah told a press conference on Friday that seven people are confirmed dead after the assault on a Greek Orthodox Church in the village of Hamoud.

⁠Twenty-seven of the ⁠wounded were receiving treatment in hospitals, he said.

The search for the gunmen is ongoing, Al-Maaytah added, pledging that “the perpetrators will be caught and our national unity will not be hit”.

Survivors said they heard an explosion when the funeral procession started, after which masked attackers broke into the church and began shooting for several minutes.

State-owned television station Al-Mamlaka reported that security forces were deployed to the church and were pursuing two suspects, who got out of a vehicle and opened fire.

Funeral attendee Khaled Burqan told Al-Mamlaka that dozens of people were at the procession. One of the assailants carried a pistol, he said, and the other carried a rifle.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the attack.

Without naming a specific group, Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya told the press conference that the “terrorist” attack was “unprecedented” and was perpetrated by a group with “no relationship to humanity”.

“This country will never be dragged into terrorism and violence,” he said, adding that “Jordanians have never seen something like this before”.

Earlier, Jordan’s King Abdullah II vowed authorities would confront the attackers “with the harshest penalties”.

“The blood of Jordanians is precious, and we will strike with an iron fist against anyone who overreaches against this country,” he said in a post on X.

The United Arab Emirates foreign ministry meanwhile condemned what it described as “terrorist and criminal acts”, and said it rejected all forms of violence “that aim to undermine security and stability”.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres also strongly condemned the attack, his spokesman Stephane Dujarric said. “It goes without saying that an attack not only on a place of worship but during a funeral procession is especially heinous,” Dujarric told reporters on Friday.

Such attacks are extremely rare in Jordan. Christians, numbering about 300,000 people, make up a minority of Jordan’s population of roughly 11.5 million, though the country is home to several biblical sites that attract Christians from around the world.

This is not the first time that Karak has come under attack.

In 2016, a deadly ISIL (ISIS) assault saw a group of fighters hole up in a Crusader-era castle and kill 10 people, including security officers and a Canadian tourist. Jordanian security forces ultimately shot and killed the attackers.

Karak, located about 120km (75 miles) south of the capital Amman, is home to “Christians and Muslims who have lived side by side for generations”, Taylor Luck, senior Middle East correspondent at the Christian Science Monitor, told Al Jazeera.

“This community prides themselves on its interfaith solidarity and coexistence,” Luck said.

If the attack was “intended to create divisions, we are likely to see this community come back even stronger”, he added.

More broadly, the shooting holds significance not just for Jordan’s Christian population, but also Amman’s “public diplomacy” as a custodian of both Christian and Muslim holy sites in Jerusalem, political analyst Xavier Abu Eid told Al Jazeera.

For years, King Abdullah has been a vocal critic of Israel’s systemic attacks against religious sites in occupied Palestinian territory.

“This is something that goes totally against the message that Jordan wants to give to the world,” Abu Eid said.

articles.title: Trump and Vance back Ramaswamy despite campaign fiasco that could damage GOP beyond Ohio
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: MAGA boss Donald Trump and his vice-president JD Vance have doubled down on supporting Indian-American Vivek Ramaswamy
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: MAGA boss Donald Trump and his vice-president JD Vance have doubled down on supporting Indian-American Vivek Ramaswamy for Governor of Ohio despite a campaign fiasco roiling the Republican party. It involves a Ramaswamy campaign ad appearing to ignore and belittle the childhood sexual abuse trauma of his Democratic opponent.The controversial ad features Donna Arthur, the birth mother of Democratic candidate Amy Acton, accusing her daughter of lying about her past and urging voters not to elect her governor. It disputes Acton’s account of childhood homelessness and abuse, without explaining the family history behind their estrangement.Also Read: Vivek Ramaswamy goes low in Ohio's race to the bottomActon, 60, has said she was sexually abused by her stepfather when she was a child and that her mother failed to protect her and continued to live with the man. She and her brother were removed from their mother’s custody, and Acton has said she has not seen her mother since childhood. Her brother, Philip Stearns, has supported her account. Court records have corroborated significant elements of the childhood trauma, and Acton has called the advertisement exploitative and deeply hurtful.Trump, who initially professed ignorance of the ad, subsequently endorsed it in emphatic terms, calling it “very powerful” in a Truth Social post and asking, “Who wouldn’t use such an Ad?” He described the controversy surrounding it as evidence that the press was trying to suppress an effective political attack, even as Vance, who was elected Senator from Ohio before his elevation as veep, told Republicans to stop complaining about it and concentrate on winning elections.The ad has freaked out many Republicans -- already on the backfoot and in danger of losing both the House and Senate -- who believe it crosses a line even by the standards of modern negative campaigning. Ohio’s outgoing Governor Mike DeWine, a Republican who has endorsed Ramaswamy, called the spot “just wrong” and urged the campaign to take it down. Former Republican presidential candidate and South Carolina Governor Nikki Haley also criticised Ramaswamy, saying, “He’s a bad guy,” and asserting that the controversy vindicated her earlier warnings about him.But the most scathing criticism came from GOP lawmaker Nancy Mace of South Carolina, who has spoken publicly about her own experience as a sexual-abuse survivor, and is one of only four Republicans who joined Democrats in demanding release of the Epstein files. “The thing with Vivek is he could have won WITHOUT that ad. Just nasty...The bar is low and somehow he managed to limbo under the lowest bar of decency in this country,” Mace said, adding that anyone defending it “needs to have their head examined.”Trump and Vance did just that. “It's a very unusual situation to have a mother hate a daughter that much, but I don't think that has anything to do with Vivek,” Trump told reporters, accepting the mother's allegations without addressing Acton's claims of childhood sexual abuse that has received sympathy nationwide. “The Press is trying to convince everyone that this Ad is bad, because it’s so good! Who wouldn’t use such an Ad? I would, it’s called, “hitting pay dirt.” Trump said.The political consequences of the ad fiasco extend beyond the governor's race in Ohio where Ramaswamy now trails Acton. It could also pull down Republican Senator Jon Husted, fighting to retain his against Democrat Sherrod Brown, a former Senator who backpacked through India in the 1970s as a young collegiate and has local Indian support.The Ohio controversy is unfolding against a deteriorating political backdrop for Trump, whose decision to campaign aggressively for Republican candidates has become a double-edged sword. At rallies in recent days Trump has continued to rely on his familiar combination of grievances, personal attacks, boasts and freewheeling digressions, all of which appeal to his hardcore MAGA base but is driving away moderates. The disconnect between Trump's rally rhetoric and the concerns dominating household budgets -- Inflation, gasoline, groceries, health care and home energy costs -- are ratting even Republicans now. Republicans hold the House 218-214 and Senate 53-47, so loss of even a 3-4 seats will result in a big upheaval in Washington DC.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Finland nearing opening of world’s first permanent nuclear waste repository
articles.summary: Facilities are being built in many countries, but Finland is the first to licence its underground storage facility.
articles.body:
Finland has granted an operating licence for the world’s first permanent underground repository for spent nuclear fuel.

The government handed Onkalo, in western Finland, the licence on Thursday, waste management company Posiva said.

Although the move does not allow the opening of the facility, it is expected to start operations soon, the firm said. However, 22 years after construction began, no exact date has been decided yet.

“This is a great and historic day for both Posiva and Finland,” the company’s Chief Executive Officer Ilkka Poikolainen said in a statement.

“Before final disposal begins, Posiva will finalise the commissioning stage, carrying out the necessary tests and inspections which STUK [the Finnish Radiation and Nuclear Safety Authority] also needs to verify and approve.”

With space for 6,500 tonnes of uranium, Onkalo, which means “cave” in Finnish, will provide permanent storage for spent fuel from Finland’s five nuclear reactors.

The fuel will be enclosed in copper canisters that are highly resistant to corrosion inside the geological repository . The canisters will then be lowered into holes drilled into the bedrock, which will be filled with bentonite clay and finally sealed with a steel-reinforced concrete plug.

The waste will remain highly radioactive for tens of thousands of years. After about 100,000 years, the levels will be about the same as the uranium ore of which the fuel is made, according to Posiva.

Countries have been wrestling with what to do with dangerous nuclear by-products since the first plants were built in the 1950s. Currently, most of it is in temporary storage.

Final repositories are being built in other countries, including neighbouring Sweden and France, but Finland is expected to be the first to open its underground storage facility.

The cost of the Onkalo site has been estimated at $1.16bn.

articles.title: Marshall Faulk, Hall of Fame running back, reveals he has Parkinson’s disease
articles.summary: Hall of Fame running back and Southern University football coach Marshall Faulk revealed that he’s been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease and hopes early detection will give him chances “at living a better quality of life.”
articles.body: Hall of Fame running back and Southern University football coach Marshall Faulk revealed that he’s been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease and hopes early detection will give him chances “at living a better quality of life.” The 53-year-old made the announcement on “The Caring Neurologist” podcast on Wednesday, telling host Dr. Sandeep Thakkar that he hopes others will look out for early symptoms in themselves. “What you want to do with that information is pass it on to the next generation to make sure that they have it better. that they know more,” Faulk said. “And you’re doing the leave this world a better place than it was, you know, when I got here.” The progressive nervous system disorder affects more than a million Americans. Faulk said he has been living with the condition for about 18 months and has experienced some hand rigidity and tremors. “I think I caught it early and I’m in a good place,” the football icon said. ”I didn’t look at it like I got a diagnosis, it was something bad that I was, you know, life was going to end. Now, if you don’t take care of it, there’s an opportunity for that to be, but you have to take care of it.” The coach is optimistic that medications can, at least in the immediate future, stave off the most serious symptoms of Parkinson’s. “The earlier you catch it, the better chance you have at living a better quality of life with medication compared to if you catch it later, then you, the things that you start to have, the things that you go through, it makes life a little bit more difficult,” he said. Faulk said he took inspiration from meeting Muhammad Ali in the boxer’s later years as the champ fought Parkinson’s. “I sat next to him and he leaned over to me and he whispered, ‘You a bad boy,’” Faulk fondly recalled of having dinner with Ali. “And then he made a couple other comments. I was like, ‘He’s all there.’” Faulk played 12 years in the NFL, seven for the then-St. Louis Rams and five for the Indianapolis Colts. He rushed for 12,279 yards, 13th most in league history. But it Faulk’s ability to catch the football which made him one of the game’s most dangerous weapons. His 19,514 total yards from scrimmage ranks 5th all-time. Faulk and his “Greatest Show on Turf” Rams won the 2000 Super Bowl, in a game best known for Mike Jones’ game-saving tackle of Kevin Dyson at the Rams’ 1-yard line as time expired. Faulk caught 5 passes for 90 yards in that game played at the Georgia Dome. The No. 2 overall pick in 1994 out of San Diego State was inducted into Canton in 2011. He is in his first season as head coach at Southern and the Jaguars are 3-4. Southern plays Saturday against Texas Southern at Reliant Stadium in Houston. Representatives for Southern could did immediately respond to an NBC News request for comment on Friday. Faulk said he’s not yet experienced any cognitive issues. Parkinson’s can bring sleep, memory, problem solving and other brain-related challenges. “My brain’s fine,” the coach said. “I feel clear of thought and I guess that’s a good thing.” Faulk said he’s aware of difficulties that could be in his future and is already taking steps to more clearly organize his thoughts. “Life has been, I want to say, normal,” the Hall of Fame running back said. “I take better notes, I’m more concise when I’m doing interviews.”

articles.title: ‘Impossible without my intervention’: Melania Trump secures Russia-Ukraine ceasefire in Oleshky
articles.summary: US First Lady Melania Trump on Friday said she had secured a local ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Ukrainian city of Oleshky, with the
articles.body: US First Lady Melania Trump on Friday said she had secured a local ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Ukrainian city of Oleshky, with the agreement set to take effect on October 29, 2026.The temporary halt in military action is intended to allow humanitarian aid to enter the city and facilitate the evacuation of civilians through a designated safe passageway.“The situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a front-line war city on the brink of disaster. Oleshky’s remaining population is comprised primarily of elderly residents who urgently need medical attention, medicine, food, and clean water,” said First Lady Melania Trump.“The people of Oleshky have limited electricity, live amid mined roads, and endure regular military attacks. It was abundantly clear that without my intervention, the possibility to bring humanitarian aid into the city and to evacuate the elderly would be impossible.”Melania Trump said she and her representative worked directly with Russian and Ukrainian leadership to establish the terms of the ceasefire, including its objectives, procedures, timing and implementation. She said she acted in her formal role as Exclusive Intermediary.“Non-military, civilian leaders from both countries will work together to visit Oleshky residents in their homes and determine the level of assistance they require. Residents who wish to evacuate will receive coordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine,” said First Lady Melania Trump.She also said she had arranged for an American media organisation to accompany Russian and Ukrainian teams during the process to document their activities.“The First Lady continued, “I have also secured an impartial American media organization to accompany and document Russian and Ukrainian teams on the ground throughout the process. This will play a significant role in ensuring that the wishes of each family are faithfully respected.”How the ceasefire initiative beganMelania Trump said she learnt about the situation in Oleshky during a private discussion at her Fostering the Future Together event in New York City, held during the 81st United Nations General Assembly.“My representative and I immediately leveraged the communication channel we established with Russia and Ukraine through the previous six reunifications of 34 children. Both nations promptly assigned teams to coordinate the complex mechanics involved, including demining. All parties have worked around the clock since that moment,” explained First Lady Melania Trump.Oleshky is located in southern Ukraine, across the Dnipro River from Kherson. Before the war, the city had a population of around 24,000. An estimated 1,700 to 2,000 residents remain, primarily older people who have been unable to leave, along with approximately 50 children.No formal demographic count has been conducted in Oleshky since 2022. The city has remained on the front line since the war began, leading to the displacement or evacuation of much of its population.Following the destruction of the Kakhovka Dam, approximately 90 per cent of the city's territory was flooded.You use AI every day. articles.title: Staffordshire roads flooded as Storm Austen hits
articles.summary: Several parts of north Staffordshire are facing flooding, as Storm Austen batters the region.
articles.body:
Areas of north Staffordshire are flooded, as Storm Austen hits the region, having battered southern parts of the UK earlier on Friday.

A slip road on the A500 for Sandyford/Tunstall saw a car stranded as motorists try to navigate difficult conditions.

Meanwhile, the Greyhound Gap dog rescue charity in Kidsgrove said they had to evacuate their dogs to an emergency shelter because their premises had flooded.

Elsewhere, Storm Austen is causing widespread power cuts and travel disruption – with wind gusts of 84mph (135km/h) recorded at Jersey Airport.

There were reports of flooding in Cross Heath and Lower Milehouse in Newcastle-under-Lyme as well as a pedestrian underpass in the town centre.

The heavy rain has also caused a manhole cover to collapse on Kidsgrove Bank South and a classic car event, which was due to take place tomorrow in Newcastle-under-Lyme, has been postponed and will now be held in November.

Parts of the Trentham estate in Stoke-on-Trent were shut because of the weather, with the site confirming they were forced to close because of the number of trees.

"We are continuing to closely monitor the high winds affecting Trentham Gardens today," a spokesperson said.

"The lakeside walk and wider gardens are currently closed as a precautionary measure, although the Italian Gardens remain open at this time."

Weather conditions will continue to be monitored throughout the weekend, and anyone planning to visit is advised to check the attraction's website first.

The shopping village area remained open, they said.

There were flood warning issued for Saredon Brook at Standeford near Coven, south Staffordshire, as well as Waterhead Brook at Bushbury, Wolverhampton.

The Environment Agency said rising river levels were expected to cause flooding throughout the evening at Saredon Brook with properties around the Stafford Road area potentially affected.

People were advised to avoid low lying footpaths and any bridges near local watercourses.

Meanwhile, at Waterhead Brook high river levels were causing flooding with properties and roads around Abbeyfield Road Wolverhampton being monitored.

People were advised to start acting on their flood plans, if they have one, with further updates expected later on Friday .

articles.title: US justice department investigating Corey Lewandowski over DHS role
articles.summary: Trump's former campaign manager is reportedly being investigated for allegedly using his role at the Department of Homeland for financial gain.
articles.body:
The US Department of Justice (DOJ) is investigating whether Corey Lewandowski, who was a top aide to former Department ⁠of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Kristi Noem, personally profited from his role, according to the BBC's US partner CBS News.

Lewandowski worked closely with Noem as a special government employee until March, when the two were both ousted after a series of controversies, including the fatal shootings of US citizens by immigration officers.

The probe is related to contracts the agency signed under Noem's leadership, a source told CBS.

The BBC has contacted Lewandowski's attorney, who told CBS his client denies any wrongdoing.

"Mr Lewandowski has not been contacted by the justice department regarding any investigation," his attorney, Adam Trigg, said.

Asked about the investigation on Thursday, President Donald Trump told reporters he had heard about it but did not know the details, adding, "I want my people to be honest".

"And if they're not going to be honest, they have to be prosecuted," he said.

Lewandowski served as a campaign manager to Trump during his first presidential run in 2016 and helped advise his 2024 campaign.

DHS officials told Reuters that Lewandowski had approved some DHS contracts despite not having the legal authority to do so as a special government employee.

He also allegedly put certain grants and contracts on hold, including some involving the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), the officials told Reuters.

Special government employees serve as temporary advisers to federal agencies and are given strict limits on how much they can work and what they can do.

The justice department took on the investigation after receiving a referral from the DHS inspector general's office, which is made up of lawyers charged with monitoring the agency's conduct and operations.

At DHS, Lewandowski served as Noem's de facto chief of staff.

Noem also faced a contract controversy. Shortly before she left office, lawmakers pressed her about the process she had used to award a $220m (£164m) advertising contract to two companies with ties to her and people in her inner circle.

The Wall Street Journal has reported that Lewandowski also allegedly tried to use his role at DHS for financial gain by asking Middle Eastern countries to hire him on the side to help with visa and other DHS issues.

articles.title: Montana conservation group bought 70,000-acre ranch once owned by Texas billionaires, expanding planned nature preserve beyond half a million acres
articles.summary: A Montana conservation group purchased a 70,000-acre ranch formerly owned by Texas billionaires, bringing its total land holdings to more than half a
articles.body: A Montana conservation group purchased a 70,000-acre ranch formerly owned by Texas billionaires, bringing its total land holdings to more than half a million acres. American Prairie announced the acquisition of Anchor Ranch in central Montana in 2025. The nonprofit aims to create the largest nature preserve in the Lower 48.According to Montana Public Radio, the ranch had been listed for about $36 million, although the organisation declined to disclose the purchase price. The acquisition also included a portion of Bullwhacker Road, a key access route to 50,000 acres of public land in the Upper Missouri River Breaks area. American Prairie said it planned to keep the route open to the public, while ranching families leasing the land would remain in place.American Prairie purchased 70,000 acres of Anchor Ranch in MontanaAmerican Prairie acquired Anchor Ranch, which was formerly owned by Texas billionaires the Wilks Brothers. The ranch was listed for about $36 million, but the nonprofit did not disclose how much it paid for the property. The purchase added 70,000 acres of land in central Montana to the organisation’s existing holdings.The acquisition brought American Prairie’s total land holdings to more than half a million acres. The group aims to establish the largest nature preserve in the Lower 48. Spokesperson Beth Saboe said, "We saw a once-in-a-generation opportunity to secure an important piece of ecologically and culturally significant land."How the ranch purchase secured access to 50,000 acres of public landThe newly acquired property included a portion of Bullwhacker Road, a primary access point to 50,000 acres of public land in the Upper Missouri River Breaks area. Access along the route had been a longstanding point of contention because former landowners had restricted its use. articles.title: Ohio father charged with killing sheriff deputy found guilty
articles.summary: An Ohio father accused of mowing down a deputy with his car hours after he viewed body camera video of a Cincinnati police officer fatally shooting his son was found guilty Friday of charges including murder.
articles.body: An Ohio father accused of mowing down a deputy with his car hours after he viewed body camera video of a Cincinnati police officer fatally shooting his son was found guilty Friday of charges including murder. The jury began deliberating Wednesday morning following days of testimony in Rodney L. Hinton’s murder trial, NBC affiliate WLWT of Cincinnati reported. Hinton is scheduled to be sentenced on November 16. Just hours before the May 2025 crash that killed Hamilton County Special Deputy Larry Henderson, Hinton had been called to the police station to watch body camera video of his 18-year-old son fatally shot by a Cincinnati officer. Police had responded to a report of a stolen vehicle at an apartment complex. Authorities said Hinton’s son, Ryan Hinton, was among a group of people in the allegedly stolen car, and some of them ran when officers approached. Two officers pursued Ryan Hinton, who police said was armed, and another person. In video released by police, an officer exits his vehicle and points his gun at Ryan Hinton, who appears to be running away. The officer fired at least four shots, police said at a news conference last year. In another video, an officer yells, “He’s got a gun!” Authorities said the gun was recovered from the scene. In closing arguments, defense attorney Clyde Bennett II said Hinton had struggled with mental health in the past and that his family was worried about him after he watched the video. Bennett asked the jury to find Hinton not guilty by reason of insanity. Prosecutors said Henderson saw the car coming at the last second and stepped out of the way, but Hinton “tracked him.” “He turned his wheel the same direction that Larry moved, and the car struck Larry, throwing him, tossing him into the air, twisting him until he landed,” Assistant Prosecutor Kate Burroughs said in closing arguments. Burroughs said Hinton’s vehicle went from 0 to over 43 mph in seconds and the accelerator was pressed 93.3%. “Everything that happened that day was in the driver’s hands,” she said. During the trial, the defense’s expert witness testified that Hinton did not know right from wrong at the time of the crash, according to WLWT. The state’s rebuttal witness testified that Hinton was grieving and angry but knew his actions were wrong. Henderson’s wife also took the stand and became emotional as she discussed their last moments together before he left for work, the news station reported. “He looked at me, and he said, ‘I love you,’ and I remember adding, I said back, ‘I love you too,’” Lori Henderson said, crying. Henderson had retired from the sheriff’s office about five months before the crash and was working as a special deputy directing traffic near the University of Cincinnati during graduation.

articles.title: Civil servant who juggled five jobs says he was 'surprised' to be charged with fraud
articles.summary: Kashim Chowdhury denied being dishonest when not telling employers he had other jobs.
articles.body:
A civil servant accused of fraudulently juggling multiple government jobs says he was ''surprised'' to have been charged with fraud.

Kashim Chowdhury told the jury at Southwark Crown Court he had not been dishonest in failing to tell his employers he had other government jobs.

"At that time I was just on auto pilot, I was like a robot, I was not thinking clearly," he said.

Chowdhury, 55, from east London, is accused of nine counts of fraud. He denies acting dishonestly or intending to make a dishonest gain.

Between 2020 and 2023 Chowdhury had eight overlapping public sector jobs. He was contractually obliged to work full time and was paid a full-time salary by each organisation. He is accused of fraudulently earning more than £284,000.

In March 2023 Chowdhury began working for the Home Office despite being under contract to work full time at the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra), the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the Department for Business and Trade and the Food Standards Agency.

The court was told he started the Home Office job while on sick leave from three of his other jobs.

Prosecuting barrister Lucy Organ asked him: "If you were really sick for work, how were you able to start your work at the Home Office?"

Chowdhury said: "I did not want this job at the Home Office, I was told there would be adequate support and I could work whatever hours I wanted to work."

Organ also asked why he did not submit a sick note to the Home Office "You were using these sick notes to be able to cope. It was all too much wasn't it?"

Chowdhury rejected the suggestion, adding: "I wanted to carry on working."

In May 2023, Chowdhury was contracted to work 183 hours a week, more than the number of hours in seven days.

He told the jury he agreed with his employers to work flexibly and that his work was project or output based. He said this was agreed "informally" via text messages but the phones used to send the texts had gone missing when his house was searched by investigators.

He said that to cope with the workload he would work from 07:00 on Saturdays and Sundays and not finish until 20:00 or 21:00.

Civil servant faked illness with make-up to juggle five jobs, court hears

Civil servant admits he 'made mistakes' juggling five government jobs

Organ asked him: "Wasn't that a bit much for you?"

"I was house bound, I was looking after my mum," he said.

The prosecution alleges Chowdhury managed to keep his overlapping jobs secret because he worked entirely remotely. He told his employers he was the sole carer for his elderly mother and the prosecution alleges he "exploited this opportunity".

His line manager at the UKHSA, Aleesha Adams, organised a video call with him in May 2023 to discuss his sick leave.

She previously told the court she was surprised when he logged on wearing white make-up because his name led her to expect to see an Asian man with darker skin.

She told the court that as the meeting went on the make-up started coming off his forehead. ''He was sweating, it was like rubbing off so it was darker underneath and darker on the neck."

But Chowdhury denied having worn make-up at the meeting

''That's a smear, I've never worn make-up in my life. At that particular time, I was suffering from anxiety and depression. I had already submitted my sick note, there was no need to put on make-up.''

articles.title: Sheffield residents react to UK City of Culture 2029 shortlisting
articles.summary: Sheffield is in the running for a £10m prize fund to deliver a year of cultural events in 2029.
articles.body:
The announcement that Sheffield has been shortlisted to become the UK's City of Culture 2029 has been broadly welcomed by people living and working there.

Blackpool, Milton Keynes and Wrexham have also been shortlisted alongside Sheffield, with the winner set to secure a £10m prize fund to deliver a year of cultural events.

Shoppers in Sheffield have told the BBC the spotlight that comes with the title would be good for the city having seen two other Yorkshire cities, Hull and Bradford, previously win the prestigious title.

Mark Dickman, 52, who lives in Fulwood, said he thought being named UK City of Culture would "put the city on the map and boost public perception of Sheffield".

He said he thought becoming City of Culture 2029 would be "a good thing", but added that regardless of the result, Sheffield could still market its culture better.

"It doesn't do a particularly great job of shouting about itself like Liverpool and Manchester does," he said.

"It does culture well internally, but not really externally. I think if you live in Sheffield you like it, but if you're from outside the city, it's not really your first port of call for a visit."

A new location is crowned UK City of Culture every four years as part of a government bid to boost pride and economic growth across the country, with the winning city due to be announced next May.

The shortlisted cities were recommended by the UK City of Culture expert advisory panel, chaired by Sir Phil Redmond, and were whittled down from nine longlist applications including Inverness-Highland, Ipswich, Middlesbrough, Portsmouth and Swindon.

The shortlisted cities will now each receive at least £125,000 to bring elements of their bids to life.

Luke Nash, who is 28, remembers the impact the City of Culture had in his native Hull, when it held the title in 2017 .

"It put a good spotlight on it when it had previously been overlooked," he says.

"I think it would be a good thing for Sheffield. There's lots of museums, galleries - and the people are great as well."

Joseph Fagan, 72, from Crookes, which was recently branded the UK's sixth coolest neighbourhood , said he thought Sheffield had as "good a chance as any" of being named City of Culture.

"The student population, I think, brings a lot of life to the city," he said.

"You've got the Peak District as well - whichever direction you go out from the city you've got great countryside."

Meanwhile, several people highlighted Sheffield's theatre and music scenes as a reason it should win the coveted prize.

Bands such as Pulp and The Arctic Monkeys famously originated from the city, while The Crucible will soon be revamped after it was recently announced the World Snooker Championship would remain in its spiritual home until 2045 .

"There's something for everyone here," said Val Newbolt, who came to Sheffield as a student from her native Sunderland.

"A lot of local musicians from here have done well. You've got the cinemas, too, and you've got the Arena, which puts on a lot of different shows."

However, she raised a slight concern about the state of the city centre, which, like many others, has seen several shop units close in recent years.

That view was echoed by 51-year-old Joanne Cartwright, who answered "yes and no" when asked if being named City of Culture would be a good thing for Sheffield.

"It feels like the city centre's taken a dive," she said.

"Covid didn't help. There's a lot of rough sleepers now and they can be quite abusive.

"But every city has its rough parts and its good parts. I do think Sheffield has a lot to offer culturally.

"I think being City of Culture would give it a boost."

Councillor Fran Belbin, leader of Sheffield City Council, told BBC Radio Sheffield the city's bid showed how the UK City of Culture 2029 title would "involve more communities, reduce inequalities in the city, increase access to the cultural centre and drive growth and regeneration".

Belbin said it was Sheffield's heritage that made it stand out against the other shortlisted locations.

"We've got our fantastic industrial heritage, with everything from Sheffield having the world's first football club to the pioneering electronic music we've produced.

"We've got internationally acclaimed theatre and neighbourhood traditions that exist across the city as well.

"We've got a really authentic and inclusive cultural identity."

"I can't speak for the other cities on the list, but I know Sheffield can deliver an absolutely fantastic experience," she added.

Speaking to BBC Radio Sheffield, listener Nick said Sheffield being named UK City of Culture 2029 would be a "no brainer".

"It's already a city of culture," he said.

"It's got museums, galleries, artwork, sporting legends."

The list of Sheffield's offerings was "endless", including food and music festivals, plenty of green space and even the National Video Game Museum, he explained.

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy called the competition an "undiluted celebration of what makes our largest towns and cities so brilliant".

"Great culture is everywhere, but the opportunity to showcase it, to put it on display and to show how it is woven into our national story is not", she added.

Research by the University of Warwick and Coventry University, previously showed that Coventry's year as City of Culture helped to generate more than £183m for the local economy .

articles.title: Ex-Tory campaign chief and his wife sentenced over election bets
articles.summary: Anthony Lee passed confidential information to his wife Laura Lee about when the 2024 general election would be held.
articles.body:
The Conservatives' former director of campaigning and his wife have received suspended prison sentences after they admitted to cheating at gambling by placing bets on the date of the 2024 general election.

Anthony Lee used "inside information" emerging from a private meeting called by then-Prime Minister Rishi Sunak to bet on the general election date months before it took place, Southwark Crown Court heard.

Lee and his wife Laura stood to win more than £23,000 had their cheating not been uncovered, the court heard.

Lee was sentenced to 10 months and two weeks' imprisonment, suspended for 12 months, while his wife was sentenced to four months and two weeks' imprisonment, suspended for a year.

Amy Hind, a former Tory party employee who was working as an NHS business support manager, was also sentenced to six months' imprisonment, suspended for a year, after previously pleading guilty to cheating on the date of the election.

Judge Tony Baumgartner, sentencing the three of them, said their conduct "risked undermining" the confidence the public has in the Conservative Party "as an institution", "undermining trust in the democratic process" and the "integrity of the gambling system".

The trio were among several people charged with betting offences by the Gambling Commission.

The trials of other defendants will take place next year and in 2028.

Former Conservative MP Craig Williams, who was Sunak's closest parliamentary aide at the time, pleaded guilty in June and will be sentenced at a later date.

Sunak's decision to call a general election for July 2024 was a surprise to many, including several Conservative MPs, who were expecting an autumn date.

The court heard that Sunak held a private Downing Street meeting on 10 March of that year to discuss possible dates.

Neither Lee nor his wife attended the meeting, but the couple began betting online on the election being held in July or between July and September, the court heard.

Prosecutor Zoe Johnson said: "Although not at Number 10, the overwhelming inference is that Anthony Lee was receiving inside information as the meeting went on and was acting upon it."

She added: "Together they were using it to make a profit for themselves."

Lee placed or tried to place 71 bets during the period, while his wife placed eight and attempted a ninth, the court heard.

Baumgartner described Anthony Lee as a "central figure" in the preparation of the general election, who sat at a group of desks within Tory HQ known as the "God Pod".

Representing Lee, barrister Richard Pratt said his client did not concretely know the working date of the election, saying it "still represented a gamble from his point of view".

The barrister told the court: "It was always possible the prime minister could change his mind."

Pratt said there "wasn't any direct manipulation" by the defendant.

Laura Lee worked for the Tories as their "head of international" and had been selected as the party candidate for Bristol North West for the election.

Baumgartner said she had no involvement in the election planning and her access to information "came predominantly" from her husband.

The court heard Hind's husband Anthony worked as a deputy digital director for the Conservatives but did not place any bets himself.

Baumgartner said Hind's husband "was party to emails relating to the forthcoming general election and was one potential source of your inside information".

The judge later said "someone else who worked within the heart of CCHQ" could have given her the "highly confidential" information.

The court heard Hind placed four bets and made three further unsuccessful attempts to place bets. The unsuccessful attempts were for £767, £700 and £750.

The judge described Hind's bets as a "clear departure from your previous betting history", noting: "Before the present offending, your largest stake had been £10.50, and only seven of your 3,399 recorded selections involved a stake of that amount."

Neither of the defendants have previous convictions and they are all of good previous character, the court heard.

Baumgartner described them all as having expressed remorse for their actions.

The trio are now subject to a 12-month prohibited activity requirement, banning them from accessing or using online gambling websites or applications.

Anthony Lee was ordered to complete 100 hours of unpaid work and pay more than £6,600 in compensation to a betting company, while Laura Lee must carry out 40 hours of unpaid work and pay £4,265.

Hind was ordered to complete 50 hours of unpaid work.

Katharine Diamond, General Counsel of regulators the Gambling Commission, reacted to the sentencing of the trio by saying "justice has been served".

She described the case as "a first of its kind" and said it demonstrated the commission's "commitment to protecting the integrity of betting markets".
